name: the crediting line
asks: Ten occasions at a height with seven met: the height is held (§5.3).

name: one short of the crediting rate
asks: Ten occasions with six met is under 70%: nothing is held there.

name: held, then given back
asks: A held height whose rate falls under 60% is given back, and says so rather than reading as never held (§5.3).

name: failing but still held
asks: Between the give-back line and the failing line a held height stays held and is marked failing.

name: under the sample floor
asks: Nine occasions, every one met, is still under the sample the standard asks for.

name: the worked reading of §6
asks: Each situation is placed once in a task, its commands read together, and gives one sample: Request from commands 1 to 3 at L3 met, Review from commands 4 and 5 at L3 not met, because command 4 drew a request for clarification (§6.2).

placements.cite: show the right answer, not just say wrong
placements.becomes: a quiz that reveals the right answer

placements.cite: on question 4 the right answer shows even when I get it right

name: a placement set aside gives no sample
asks: Where the placement in a situation failed for a cause of its own as its whole outcome, the task gives that situation no sample, and the escape is still counted (§5.4, §6.2).

name: question held alone is not a level
asks: Question is counted and held at its own height like any situation, and held alone it is no level: a level is held only in every conferring situation (B.2).

name: a level is held in every conferring situation
asks: L2 held in all four conferring situations is L2 held (B.2 Held).

name: three of the four conferring situations is not a level
asks: A level is held only where EVERY conferring situation holds it, and Question is one of the four (B.2 Held, B.2 Conferring).

name: short in one situation is not held
asks: Two situations at L2 and a third one occasion short holds nothing.

name: heights are counted on their own
asks: A height is held on its own samples; the heights under it are not filled in for it (§5.3, and the note in §5.1).
